english.notes:
(i) Section 19 of the Contempt of Court Act 1981 provides that "Superior Court" means the Court of Appeal, the High Court, the Crown Court, the Courts-Martial Appeal Court, the Restrictive Practices Court, the Employment Appeal Tribunal and any other court exercising in relation to its proceedings powers equivalent to those of the High Court, and includes the Supreme Court in the exercise of its appellate jurisdiction.
(ii) Section 8(3) of the Contempt of Court Act 1981 provides that this offence does not apply to any disclosure of any particulars:
(a) in the proceedings in question for the purpose of enabling the jury to arrive at their verdict, or in connection with the delivery of that verdict, OR
(b) in evidence in any subsequent proceedings for an offence alleged to have been committed in relation to the jury in the first mentioned proceedings, OR
to the publication of any particulars so disclosed.
(iii) Section 8(3) of the Contempt of Court Act 1981 provides that proceedings for a contempt of court under this section (other than Scottish proceedings) shall not be instituted except by or with the consent of the Attorney General or on the motion of a court having jurisdiction to deal with it.
(iv) Section 14(1) of the Contempt of Court Act 1981 provides that in any case where a court has power to commit a person to prison for contempt of court and (apart from this provision) no limitation applies to the period of committal, the committal shall (without prejudice to the power of the court to order his earlier discharge) be for a fixed term and that term shall not on any occasion exceed two years in the case of committal by a superior court.
(v) Section 14(4A) of the Contempt of Court Act 1981 provides that for the purposes of section 14 the county court shall be treated as a superior court.Therefore this wording also applies to the county court.
